To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the linguistic environment of children in the kindergarten is constituted of the interactions with peers and with the early education specialists.

children with a high level of communicative competence have a high level of linguistic competence, and that children with a low level of communicative and linguistic competence can improve their skills if they have access to peer interaction and the support of the early education specialists.

children’s linguistic and communicative development is closely related to their access to peer interaction, and that the quality of peer interaction is strongly influenced by the quality of the relationship between children and early educators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how the language acquisition of children in the German kindergarten is influenced by the interaction with peers and early education specialists.

the question of whether and to what extent peer interaction and the quality of interaction between children and adults influence the development of linguistic and communicative skills of children in preschools.
the question of how the peer interaction in German preschools contributes to the acquisition of language competencies in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the linguistic competencies and communicative competences of children in preschool are influenced in a complex way by various factors, such as the linguistic environment, the social situation, and the personality of children.
children who are able to communicate with each other in complex linguistic expressions are also capable of doing so with adults.
the linguistic environment in German kindergartens is not only constituted of the interaction between children, but also of the interaction between teachers and children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peer interaction plays an important role for language acquisition in preschools.
peer interaction is a key element in the development of linguistic and communicative competence.

children with a high degree of communicative competence are able to establish peer relationships and that children with a low level of communicative competence can also develop complex linguistic expressions if they are particularly interested in an issue or if the early childhood education specialists succeed in creating a situation of “shared thinking” (Sirij-Blatchford, Sylva, Melhuish, Sammons, Taggart, 2004).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of peer interaction and interaction with the early education specialists is crucial to the development of children’s linguistic and social skills.
the early childhood education specialists are the most important language models in German kindergartens.
the quality of peer interaction and the quality of interaction between children and the early education specialist are the main factors in language acquisition.
